compiled_state.author: Joe Oakhart
compiled_state.description:
A successful run that does not await pull request close never persists a terminal execution state, so it holds a platform concurrency slot until the orphan reconciler cancels it and mislabels the success.

In _promote, when params.await_pr_close is false, draft_pull_request.py returns the promoted outcome at line 2323 without a further persist call. The last state written is PR_CREATED at line 2287. count_active_runs and active_workflow both treat any state outside COMPLETED, FAILED and CANCELLED as active, so the finished run keeps consuming a slot against the platform cap. The orphan reconciler eventually reclaims it, which frees the slot but records a successful run as CANCELLED in the execution row and the audit trail.

Observed on execution intake-ee0f760a, which produced pull request 22 and finished, then appeared in the audit trail as cancelled.

Deciding the terminal state is part of this work. COMPLETED matches the outcome but has to be checked against the pull request webhook resolver in services/orchestration/webhook/pr_events.py, which selects non-terminal rows to find a workflow to signal. On this path the workflow has already returned, so there is nothing left to signal and excluding the row is expected rather than harmful. Confirm that before choosing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The promotion path that does not await close persists a terminal execution state before returning
- [ ] A run that awaits close is unchanged and still persists AWAITING_PR_CLOSE
- [ ] The pull request close resolver still finds a workflow to signal for a run that awaits close
- [ ] A finished run on the path that does not await close no longer counts toward the active run cap

## Testing
Add unit tests under tests/unit covering the promotion path with await_pr_close false and true, then run `pytest tests/unit -q` and `ruff check .`.
compiled_state.title: Persist a terminal execution state when a run does not await pull request close
